newsitem.title: USA: CEL-SCI begins HIV trial of Multikine.
newsitem.headline: CEL-SCI begins HIV trial of Multikine.

text.p: CEL-SCI Corp said Tuesday it had begun clinical trials of an immunotherapy drug for HIV-infected patients already taking so-called cocktails of protease inhibitor and anti-viral drugs.
CEL-SCI said the purpose of the study is to evaluate the safety of its drug "Multikine" with HIV patients and determine its effect on various immune system responses.

Patients must be on a stable antiviral regime and cannot change the regimen during their three-month participation in the outpatient study, to be conducted jointly with the AIDS Research Alliance in Los Angeles, CEL-SCI said.
Multikine is a natural mixture of human immune system regulators called cytokines, the company said, including Interleukin-2 and interferons.
CEL-SCI said the drug is currently in clinical trials in patients with head and neck cancer and prostate cancer.

In a separate statement, the company said its common stock -- currently listed on the Nasdaq Small Capitalization Market -- will begin trading Thursday on the American Stock Exchange under the symbol HIV.
